name: semantic-preserving bounded segmentation with capped crosscheck redundancy
purpose: Predefine how the historical evidence corpus is divided before any evaluator chooses batches, while allowing the evaluator to decide how those fixed segments should be grouped and selectively crosschecked.

heuristic.principle: Create the smallest stable evidence units that preserve local meaning without allowing file boundaries to force oversized model contexts.
preferred_boundary_order: JSON array/object member boundary when recoverable without changing source text
hard UTF-8 byte boundary only as a last resort
justification: Historical files vary greatly in size, so file-level assignment creates pathological context amplification.
Stable semantic boundaries reduce the chance that a requirement, commit, or persisted record is split mid-unit.
A hard byte ceiling bounds the largest indivisible model input even when a source has no useful structural delimiters.
Base segmentation contains no overlap; redundancy is introduced only by explicit crosscheck assignments so it can be measured and audited.

batch_constraints.per_primary_batch_rule: For P primary batches and raw corpus size D, each primary batch must contain no more than D/P raw segment bytes. The planner may increase P when this bound cannot be met.
batch_constraints.crosscheck_rule: Crosscheck batches may intentionally overlap or redistribute segments, including deterministic or seeded stochastic selection, but all repeated raw bytes count against the extra 0.5D redundancy budget.

evaluation_pipeline: lead evaluator groups fixed segments into primary batches and crosscheck batches
validate coverage and byte-budget invariants before any batch evaluation
evaluate each primary batch exactly once
evaluate each crosscheck batch exactly once
synthesize only compact batch outputs; do not resend raw corpus
prohibited: recursive Gemini calls from within a batch evaluation
model-directed compute request loops that resend the same raw context
whole-audit restart after a later batch failure
implicit overlap not represented in the batch plan
